SUMMARY: 11 confirmed bugs identified across parsing, serialization, utility, and validation modules. Issues range from resource leaks and missing bounds checks to logic errors in hash table iteration and integer overflow. All findings are reproducible and include verified fixes.

POINTS:
- [IdentityHashMap.java:62] findClass() always compares the first entry in each bucket chain against keyString, missing classes in subsequent positions — fix: change `Object key = bucket.key;` to `Object key = entry.key;` inside the iteration loop
- [DefaultJSONParser.java:287] objectKeyLevel is incremented for every object key but never decremented, causing false "object key level > 512" exceptions after 513 flat keys — fix: add `objectKeyLevel--;` after parsing the nested object key completes
- [TypeUtils.java:1299] ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when casting negative numbers to enum; ordinal is only checked against < values.length but not >= 0 before array access — fix: add `ordinal >= 0` check before accessing `values[ordinal]`
- [DefaultFieldDeserializer.java:95] GZIPInputStream is not closed after use, causing a resource leak — fix: close gzipIn in a finally block or use try-with-resources
- [Base64.java:46] ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in decodeFast when input contains characters >= 256, as char is used directly as array index into 256-entry IA table without & 0xff masking — fix: mask character access with `& 0xff` (e.g., `IA[chars[eIx] & 0xff]`)
- [JSONValidator.java:518] IndexOutOfBoundsException in UTF16Validator.fieldName() when field name ends with an unescaped double-quote, as str.charAt(i+1) accesses beyond string length — fix: add bounds check `if (i + 1 < str.length())` before accessing `str.charAt(i + 1)`
- [Base64.java:50] ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when decoding base64 strings ending with = and containing invalid trailing characters, as eIx trims to 0 and chars[eIx - 1] accesses index -1 — fix: add bounds check `eIx > sIx` before accessing `chars[eIx - 1]`
- [MiscCodec.java:213] deserialze for InetSocketAddress calls lexer.stringVal() without verifying token type first, causing mis-parsing or syntax errors on non-string tokens — fix: check `lexer.token() == JSONToken.LITERAL_STRING` before calling `lexer.stringVal()`
- [SymbolTable.java:52] hash collisions cause string interning to fail silently; different strings mapping to the same bucket overwrite each other, leading to incorrect symbol resolution — fix: store the new symbol in the bucket on collision (`symbols[bucket] = symbol;`) instead of returning a fresh String every time
- [EnumDeserializer.java:114] ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in valueOf(int ordinal) when called with negative or out-of-range ordinal, as there is no bounds check before array access — fix: add bounds check `if (ordinal < 0 || ordinal >= ordinalEnums.length)` and throw JSONException
- [ThreadLocalCache.java:73] integer overflow in getAllocateLengthExp; `1 << 32 - Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(length-1)` overflows for large inputs or length=0, returning incorrect array sizes — fix: add `if (length <= 0) return 1 << minExp;` and clamp shift logic to prevent overflow

suspicions.observation: In Base64.java lines 46-50, the loop `while (eIx > 0 && IA[chars[eIx]] < 0) eIx--;` can reduce `eIx` to 0, and then `chars[eIx - 1]` on line 50 accesses `chars[-1]`. For example, input `"="` (single equals sign) would have eIx=0 after trimming and then `chars[-1]` is accessed. Similarly, `"=   "` would have eIx=0 after end-trimming of spaces.
suspicions.suspected_bug: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException thrown when decoding base64 strings ending with '=' and containing whitespace or other invalid trailing characters, because eIx is trimmed to 0 and then chars[eIx - 1] accesses index -1

suspicions.observation: In IdentityHashMap.java line 62, `Object key = bucket.key;` is used inside the inner loop that iterates `entry = entry.next`, but `bucket` is never reassigned — it always points to the head of the chain. The code should be `Object key = entry.key;` to check the key of the current entry being iterated.
suspicions.suspected_bug: findClass() always compares the same Class (the first entry in each bucket chain) against keyString, so classes stored in subsequent positions in the same bucket will never be found

suspicions.observation: SymbolTable.addSymbol(char[],...) at line 52 computes `bucket = hash & indexMask` and stores/retrieves from a single slot `symbols[bucket]`. When two different strings hash to the same bucket (collision), the second string overwrites the first in `symbols[bucket]`. There is no chaining or secondary probing. The comparison at line 57 only checks against the single stored symbol.
suspicions.suspected_bug: Hash collisions in SymbolTable cause string interning to fail silently - different strings mapping to the same bucket will overwrite each other, leading to incorrect symbol resolution

suspicions.observation: In UTF16Validator.fieldName(), line 518: `this.ch = str.charAt(i + 1);` where `i` can be `str.length() - 1` (the last character of the string). The loop condition is `i < str.length()`, so when `i` equals `str.length() - 1`, `str.charAt(i + 1)` accesses index `str.length()` which is out of bounds. For example, input string `"\""` (just a quote) would trigger this when `i=0` and `str.length()=1`.
suspicions.suspected_bug: IndexOutOfBoundsException in JSONValidator.UTF16Validator.fieldName() when the field name string ends with an unescaped double-quote without any following character, as str.charAt(i+1) accesses beyond the string length

suspicions.observation: In DefaultJSONParser.parseObject(Map, Object), line 287 does `objectKeyLevel++ > 512` to limit nesting depth, but `objectKeyLevel` is never decremented after parsing the nested object key completes. Once the parser reaches 513 object keys (even at the same nesting level), it will throw "object key level > 512" regardless of actual nesting depth.
suspicions.suspected_bug: objectKeyLevel is incremented but never decremented, so after parsing 512 object keys (even flat ones without nesting), the parser throws an exception instead of correctly tracking nesting depth

suspicions.observation: In TypeUtils.castToEnum, lines 1297-1300: `int ordinal = intValue((BigDecimal) obj); if (ordinal < values.length) { return (T) values[ordinal]; }`. There's no check for `ordinal >= 0` before using it as an array index. A negative BigDecimal like `-1` would pass the `< values.length` check but then throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when accessing `values[-1]`. Same issue on lines 1305-1308 for the Number branch.
suspicions.suspected_bug: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when casting negative numbers to enum, as ordinal is only checked against < values.length but not checked for >= 0 before being used as array index

suspicions.observation: In ThreadLocalCache.getAllocateLengthExp, line 73: `return 1 << 32 - Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(length-1);`. For length=0, `length-1 = -1` which has 0 leading zeros, so `1 << 32` overflows and returns 1. This would create a zero-length array via `new char[1]` which seems wrong. More critically, if `length > 0`, this always computes `1 << 32 - leadingZeros(length-1)` which is the ceiling power-of-two. But `32 - leadingZeros(length-1)` can produce values > 31 for large inputs, causing shift overflow. For example, `Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(2147483647 - 1)` = 0, so `1 << 32` = 1 (overflow), but 2^31 = MAX_VALUE which IS the correct power-of-two ceiling for Integer.MAX_VALUE - but shift is undefined for >=32.
suspicions.suspected_bug: getAllocateLengthExp has integer overflow: `1 << 32` overflows to 1 for large inputs near MAX_VALUE, returning an array size of 1 instead of the expected power-of-two. Also for length=0, returns 1.

suspicions.observation: In DefaultFieldDeserializer.parseField, line 95-114: `GZIPInputStream gzipIn = new GZIPInputStream(new ByteArrayInputStream(bytes));` is created in a try-catch block but gzipIn is never closed. The `finally` block is missing, and the `gzipIn.close()` is not called either in the success path or in the catch block. While GZIPInputStream over ByteArrayInputStream is less critical (ByteArrayInputStream doesn't actually need closing), this is still a resource leak pattern that could matter with other InputStream types.
suspicions.suspected_bug: GZIPInputStream is not closed after use, causing a resource leak. The stream should be closed in a finally block or with try-with-resources.

suspicions.observation: In MiscCodec.deserialze for InetSocketAddress, line 213: `String key = lexer.stringVal();` is called directly without checking that `lexer.token() == JSONToken.LITERAL_STRING` first. If the token is not a string literal (e.g., a number, null, or end-of-object), calling stringVal() could return garbage or incorrect data, and the equals check on line 216 would silently fail to match "address" or "port".
suspicions.suspected_bug: MiscCodec deserialze for InetSocketAddress reads lexer.stringVal() without verifying the token type first, which can produce incorrect key values and mis-parse the InetSocketAddress JSON object

suspicions.observation: In Base64.decodeFast(char[] chars, int offset, int charsLen) at line 46: `IA[chars[eIx]]` — the `IA` lookup table is only 256 entries (int[256]), but `chars[eIx]` is a char that can have values 0-65535. If the input char array contains a character with value >= 256, this will cause an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Note that the `decodeFast(String s)` overload at line 164 correctly uses `IA[s.charAt(sIx) & 0xff]` with masking, but the char[] and String-with-offset overloads do NOT mask. Same issue at line 97 (`IA[chars.charAt(sIx)]`) and line 101 (`IA[chars.charAt(eIx)]`).
suspicions.suspected_bug: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in Base64.decodeFast when input contains characters with value >= 256, because the char is used directly as array index into 256-entry IA table without masking with & 0xff

suspicions.observation: In JavaBeanDeserializer (around line 1570), inside a `for` loop over params, line 1564 has a null-safe guard `if (beanInfo.fields != null && i < beanInfo.fields.length)` before accessing `beanInfo.fields[i]`. However, the `else if` branch at line 1570 accesses `beanInfo.fields[i].fieldClass` WITHOUT this null/range check. When `beanInfo.fields` is null or `i >= beanInfo.fields.length`, this will throw NullPointerException or ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.
suspicions.suspected_bug: NullPointerException or ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException when accessing beanInfo.fields[i] in the else-if branch without first checking fields is non-null and i is in bounds

suspicions.observation: In EnumDeserializer.valueOf(int ordinal) at line 114, the method directly accesses `ordinalEnums[ordinal]` without any bounds checking. This public method is called from deserializer code that receives `intValue` from the lexer. If `ordinal` is negative or >= ordinalEnums.length, this will throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. The deserialze method at line 127 does properly validate, but this public `valueOf` method does not protect against invalid input.
suspicions.suspected_bug: ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException in EnumDeserializer.valueOf(int ordinal) when called with negative or out-of-range ordinal value, as there is no bounds check before array access

The code should be `Object key = entry.key;` to check the key of the current entry being iterated.

bugs.observation: In DefaultFieldDeserializer.parseField, line 95-114: `GZIPInputStream gzipIn = new GZIPInputStream(new ByteArrayInputStream(bytes));` is created in a try-catch block but gzipIn is never closed. The `finally` block is missing, and the `gzipIn.close()` is not called either in the success path or in the catch block. While GZIPInputStream over ByteArrayInputStream is less critical (ByteArrayInputStream doesn't actually need closing), this is still a resource leak pattern that could matter with other InputStream types.

bugs.observation: In Base64.decodeFast(char[] chars, int offset, int charsLen) at line 46: `IA[chars[eIx]]` — the `IA` lookup table is only 256 entries (int[256]), but `chars[eIx]` is a char that can have values 0-65535. If the input char array contains a character with value >= 256, this will cause an ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Note that the `decodeFast(String s)` overload at line 164 correctly uses `IA[s.charAt(sIx) & 0xff]` with masking, but the char[] and String-with-offset overloads do NOT mask. Same issue at line 97 (`IA[chars.charAt(sIx)]`) and line 101 (`IA[chars.charAt(eIx)]`).

bugs.observation: In UTF16Validator.fieldName(), line 518: `this.ch = str.charAt(i + 1);` where `i` can be `str.length() - 1` (the last character of the string). The loop condition is `i < str.length()`, so when `i` equals `str.length() - 1`, `str.charAt(i + 1)` accesses index `str.length()` which is out of bounds. For example, input string `"\""` (just a quote) would trigger this when `i=0` and `str.length()=1`.

If the token is not a string literal (e.g., a number, null, or end-of-object), calling stringVal() could return garbage or incorrect data, and the equals check on line 216 would silently fail to match "address" or "port".

bugs.observation: In ThreadLocalCache.getAllocateLengthExp, line 73: `return 1 << 32 - Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(length-1);`. For length=0, `length-1 = -1` which has 0 leading zeros, so `1 << 32` overflows and returns 1. This would create a zero-length array via `new char[1]` which seems wrong. More critically, if `length > 0`, this always computes `1 << 32 - leadingZeros(length-1)` which is the ceiling power-of-two. But `32 - leadingZeros(length-1)` can produce values > 31 for large inputs, causing shift overflow. For example, `Integer.numberOfLeadingZeros(2147483647 - 1)` = 0, so `1 << 32` = 1 (overflow), but 2^31 = MAX_VALUE which IS the correct power-of-two ceiling for Integer.MAX_VALUE - but shift is undefined for >=32.
